cohort: The cohort consisted of patients with pregnancy-associated gastric cancer diagnosed between 1991 and 2012, along with two age-, sex-, and stage-matched controls for each case.
finding: The study found that the dismal prognosis of pregnancy-associated gastric cancer is more related to tumor stage and location (corpus or entire stomach) than to pregnancy status itself.
